note: HAND WRITTEN, NEVER GENERATED. This file is the honesty surface of the conformance measurement. `documentation/conformance/result.json` is what a run observes; this is what a reviewer says should be observed, and the run fails when the two disagree IN EITHER DIRECTION: a pair declared conformant that starts failing is a regression, and a pair declared non-conformant that stops failing is a stale excuse. Do not regenerate this file, and do not delete a line to make a run go green: the remedy for a broken claim is to fix the transform or to change the claim on purpose, with a reason.

DiagnosticReport.reason: The package publishes two DiagnosticReport profiles, one for laboratory results and one for clinical notes. The corpus carries one DiagnosticReport, from the ORU_R01, whose OBR-4 is a LOINC laboratory order and whose OBX results are laboratory values, so the laboratory profile is the one that applies.

DocumentReference.reason: The package publishes two DocumentReference profiles, the general one and one scoped to advance-directive documents. The corpus carries one DocumentReference, from the MDM_T02, whose TXA-2 document type is a discharge summary and not an advance directive, so the general profile is the one that applies.

Observation.reason: Every Observation profile the package publishes is topic-scoped, so no resource can satisfy them all and applying them all would measure conformance to a set nothing can conform to. How many it publishes is printed beside this reason, read off the package itself rather than written here. The default applied is the package's own catch-all for observations no other profile covers.

ORU_R01.reason: The ORU_R01's three Observations are laboratory results, each carrying a LOINC code and a quantity, so the laboratory-result profile applies to them rather than the catch-all.

The header carries the eventCoding and source R4 require, and US Core publishes nothing to hold it to beyond that.
PID-3 here names an assigning authority the transform resolves to an identifier system, so the profile's identifier slice is satisfied along with name, gender and birthDate.

Two findings. US Core requires `Encounter.type` (1..*) and the guide's PV1 map publishes no row that grounds one, so the library emits none rather than a guessed value. And US Core requires `Encounter.identifier.system`, while the library reads PV1-19's value only and never its assigning authority, so the visit-number identifier ships with a type and a value and no system. This phase measures; it does not change the mapping.
US Core requires `RelatedPerson.active` (1..1). NK1 publishes no row for it, so the library leaves it absent rather than asserting a contact is active.
AL1 grounds the clinical status, the code and the patient reference the profile requires.

So the Appointment is booked with no start, which R4 forbids. US Core publishes no Appointment profile, so base R4 is the whole measurement here.

This message's PID-3 names its assigning authority with the universal id `3.4.5.6.7` and type ISO, and that is not a well-formed OID (an OID's root arc is 0, 1 or 2). The transform therefore refuses to synthesize an identifier system from it rather than emitting a wrong one, so the identifier ships with a type and a value and no `system`, which US Core requires. Four of the other messages carry an authority that IS a well-formed OID and do get a system, which is why this claim differs by message rather than being a property of the Patient map.
The same two findings as the ADT_A01 Encounter: no `Encounter.type` the PV1 map grounds, and a visit-number identifier the library never gives a system.

Three findings, all one cause. US Core's laboratory report profile requires a `category` and a laboratory slice within it, and its us-core-9 invariant requires a result or a presented form. The guide's OBR map publishes no row that grounds a report category, so the library emits none rather than asserting the report is a laboratory one on its own authority.

All three Observations carry the same finding: US Core's laboratory profile requires `Observation.category` with a laboratory slice, and the guide's OBX map publishes no row that grounds an observation category.
